title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: A is a Dedekind ring with fraction field K, and σ is an A-order in a central simple K-algebra. The model case is a maximal order in a quaternion algebra, with A = Z and σ ramified at p and ∞.

(1) The 'Deuring category' C (with 'Picard' added in parentheses) is identified with P(σ/A), the category of locally free rank-one (projective) σ-modules. The name and the equivalence C ≃ P(σ/A) suggest the categorical form of the Deuring correspondence. That correspondence identifies supersingular elliptic curves, with isogenies, with invertible modules over a maximal quaternion order via E ↦ Hom(E0, E). The page itself only writes the abstract side.

(2) Let Brd C be the monoidal groupoid of invertible σ-σ-bimodules (two-sided invertible ideals). 'Brd' is presumably for Brandt. It acts on C by tensor product. Hence Brd(C) = π0(Brd C) acts on Is(C), the set of left-ideal classes. Here Brd(C) is the Picent of Fröhlich, or Pic_A(σ) of Bass.
- The question posed: describe the set of isomorphism classes of A-algebras 'apparentées' (related) to σ, i.e. the endomorphism rings End(X) for X in C. This is the set of types in the genus of σ.
- Claim: the stabiliser of a class X under Brd(C) is the outer automorphism group Out(σ) = Aut_A(σ)/Inn(σ). It is written Ext(σ), 'automorphismes extérieurs'.

(3) Exact sequence: 0 → A* → σ* → Aut_A σ → Brd(C) → Is C → Is O → 0. The identifications are:
- A* = π1 of Brd C (the centre's units);
- σ* = Aut_C(X) = π1(C, X);
- Is C = π0(C);
- O = groupoid of algebras related to σ, so π0(O) = types.

(4) The structure is made explicit with three groupoids: the Brandt groupoid B (with unit object 1), the Deuring groupoid C (with X), and the groupoid O of related orders (with σ = End X). The boxed sequence is
0 → π1(B,1) → π1(C,X) → π1(O,σ) → π0(B,1) → π0(C,X) → π0(O,σ) → 1.
It is the homotopy long exact sequence of the functor End: C → O. Its fibre over σ is a torsor under the 2-group B. Grothendieck: 'On a envie de dire que C est fibrée sur O, de fibre B.' In modern terms, C → O is a fibration of groupoids (or B-torsor / B-gerbe-like object) with fibre the Picard 2-group B. The sequence is R. Brown's exact sequence for fibrations of groupoids.

(5) The Picard groupoid of A maps to B by M ↦ M⊗σ. This gives π1(B,1) = π1(Pic A) = A*, and the exact sequence Pic(A) → π0(B,1) → Ram(C/A) → 0. Grothendieck names Ram(C/A) the 'ramification group of C over A' and states Ram ≅ ⊕_p Z/e_p Z in the Deuring–Brandt case.
- This matches the classical fact that two-sided ideals of a maximal order are generated by central ideals and primes P_p with P_p^{e_p} = pσ. For quaternions, e_p = 2 at ramified p.
- The boxed marginal note 'Br(K_p)/Br(A_p)' points to a general description: e_p is the order of the local class of the algebra in Br(K_p)/Br(A_p), i.e. of its residue at p.

Purpose: a categorical, homotopical reformulation of the Eichler/Deuring/Brandt theory of class numbers versus type numbers of orders. It probably serves the motive programme over finite fields: supersingular curves and endomorphism algebras as Tate-type data.
errors: The stabiliser of [X] under Brd(C) equals the image of Aut_A σ, i.e. Out_A(σ) = Aut_A σ/Inn σ, directly from exactness. The stated hypothesis 'si Brd(A)=0' (or Pic(A)/Br(A)=0; the word is hard to read) seems unnecessary for this identification. It might be needed only if 'automorphisms' means non-A-linear ring automorphisms, or to compare with the action of Pic(A).
Exactness at the π0 terms is in the sense of pointed sets with a group action, not groups. Is C and Is O are not groups in general; the final '→ 0 / → 1' should be read as surjectivity of sets.

'Ram ≅ ⊕ Z/e_p' presupposes σ maximal (hereditary at least). For non-maximal orders (e.g. Eichler orders) the two-sided ideal group is more complicated (Atkin–Lehner-type elements). Grothendieck restricts to 'le cas Deuring–Brandt'.
The fibration claim is left heuristic ('on a envie de dire'). In fact B acts on C over O and the fibres are B-torsors, so it is a genuine fibration of groupoids, but no proof is written.

ideas.what: Deuring category C equivalent to the category of rank-one projective modules over an order σ (C ≃ P(σ/A))
ideas.modern_name: Categorical Deuring correspondence (supersingular elliptic curves ↔ invertible right modules over a maximal quaternion order)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (1941) for the bijection; categorical equivalence formalised by Kohel (1996 thesis) and Voight (Quaternion Algebras, 2021, ch. 42)

ideas.what: Exact sequence A* → σ* → Aut_A σ → Picent(σ) → classes → types
ideas.modern_name: Rosenberg–Zelinsky / Bass / Fröhlich exact sequence for Picent and the class/type relation of orders
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rosenberg–Zelinsky (1961), Bass (Algebraic K-theory, 1968), Fröhlich (1973); class vs type numbers: Eichler, Deuring

ideas.what: Interpretation as the homotopy long exact sequence of a fibration of groupoids C → O with fibre the Brandt 2-group B of invertible bimodules
ideas.modern_name: Fibration of groupoids / 2-group (Picard groupoid) torsor; Brown's exact sequence; stacky (groupoid) view of the genus of an order
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Brown (1970) for groupoid fibration sequences; groupoid-of-ideals viewpoint goes back to Brandt (1927); stacky treatments of quaternion class sets are recent (various)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses groupoids and Picard categories in general, but not this application

ideas.what: Ram(C/A) := Picent(σ)/im Pic(A) ≅ ⊕_p Z/e_p, with e_p linked to Br(K_p)/Br(A_p)
ideas.modern_name: Two-sided ideal group of a maximal order modulo central ideals; local indices via Brauer residues
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hasse, Deuring, Eichler; Auslander–Goldman (1960); Reiner, Maximal Orders §22

missed.claim: Grothendieck recasts the classical Brandt-groupoid / class-number / type-number theory of quaternion orders as a homotopy long exact sequence of a fibration of groupoids (Deuring groupoid over the groupoid of related orders, fibre the Brandt 2-group). This explicitly closes the circle with Brandt's original 1927 invention of groupoids for exactly this purpose. The literature on orders (Fröhlich, Reiner, Voight) uses the exact sequences but rarely the fibration/2-group formulation.
missed.quote: On a envie de dire que C est fibrée sur O, de fibre B
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The stacky viewpoint naturally yields mass formulas as groupoid cardinalities. It also fits modern isogeny-graph and quaternion-algebra computations (Deuring correspondence in isogeny cryptography). This 1965 formulation predates Kohel/Voight's categorical Deuring correspondence.

missed.claim: A sketch defines a 'ramification group' Ram(C/A) and links it, in a boxed note, to Br(K_p)/Br(A_p). This suggests a general definition of ramification of a Deuring-type category over a base via Brauer residues, beyond the quaternion case. It is not developed.
missed.quote: Ram(C/A) « groupe de ramification de C sur A » ≃ ∐_p Z/e_pZ dans le cas Deuring–Brandt ... Br(K_p)/Br(A_p)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a modest generalisation. The relation of e_p to the order of the Brauer residue is known for maximal orders (Auslander–Goldman, Reiner), so the novelty is mainly the categorical packaging.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics (Picent sequences, class/type numbers, ⊕Z/e_p) is classical. Notable are the early (1965) categorical Deuring equivalence and the explicit fibration-of-groupoids/2-group reading of Brandt's theory, inside the motives notes. That is a nice unpublished framing but not a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: Two terms in the first exact sequence: the first is 𝒪^* (identified as A*, the centre's units), the second σ^*; the labels above the arrows (Z*?) are uncertain.
'catégorie des algèbres [?]' under Is 𝒪 likely reads 'catégorie des algébroïdes' or 'des algèbres', with 'π0(𝒪) = apparentées à σ'.
'Ext(σ)' is Grothendieck's notation for outer automorphisms ('automorphismes extérieurs'), not an Ext group.
In the condition 'si [-Brd-] Brd(A)=0' the second word is uncertain (could be Pic(A) or Br(A)).
The left-margin note near the boxed sequence probably reads something like 'en fait, fibration...'. It is largely illegible.
